To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clofibrate treatment causes a shift in the lipid composition of mouse and rat liver peroxisomal membranes towards an enrichment of unsaturated fatty acids and phosphatidyl-choline.

peroxisomes are rich in phosphatidylethenolamine, that the fatty acid composition is species-dependent, and that clofibrate treatment increases the concentrations of unsaturated long-chain phospholipids.

clofibrate causes an increase in the concentration of phosphatidyl-choline, an increase in the amount of unsaturated long-chain saturated fatty acids, and a decrease in triglycerides and cholesterol in peroxisomal membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of clofibrate on the lipid content of liver peroxises.
the effect of peroxisomal proliferation on lipid composition in peroxisomal membranes and on lipid composition of intraperoxisomal lipoproteins.
the effects of clofibrate on the lipid composition of mouse and rat liver peroxisomal membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
peroxisomal lipid metabolism is differentially regulated in mice and rats and that clofibrate treatment has differential effects on lipid metabolism in the peroxises from these species.
clofibrate treatment caused a shift from a phosphatidylethanoline- and triglyceride-rich peroxisome to a phosphatidyl-choline-rich peroxisomal structure.

peroxisomal phospholipids are more similar between mice and rats than the phospholipids in the rest of the liver, and that clofibrate treatment induces a similar change in the peroxisonal lipid composition in both species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

clofibrate treatment causes changes in the lipid composition in peroxisomal membranes, which are reflected in the lipid profiles of the membrane-associated and membrane-free lipid fractions of the organelle.

clofibrate treatment causes a change in peroxisomal lipid composition towards a phospholipid-rich and a free fatty acid-poor profile, and a change in the fatty acid pattern towards a more unsaturated profile.
the peroxisomal membrane is composed of a high proportion of phosphatidyl-ethanolamine, which contains mainly saturated fatty acids of 18 and 16 carbon atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

clofibrate treatment of mice and rats causes changes in the lipid composition of peroxisomes that are consistent with a role for the peroxisome in the regulation of the metabolism of long-chain unsaturated fatty acids and in the metabolism of cholesterol and triglycerides.
peroxisomes are highly enriched with unsaturated long-chain phosphatidylethanoline and phosphatidylcholesterol, which is in line with previous studies.
the lipid composition of peroxisomes in liver is highly dependent on the species and the nutritional status.
